newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco board set to vote on stadium bonds.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco board set to vote on stadium bonds.

text.p: San Francisco's Board of Supervisors next week will consider a resolution that would place up to a $100 million bond measure on the ballot to help build a proposed football stadium and retail complex.
Earlier this week, the board's finance committee recommended that the full board approve the proposal, which would place the lease-revenue bond measure on the June 3 special election ballot.

If approved by the Board of Supervisors at its meeting on Tuesday and by San Francisco voters in June, the ballot proposition would authorize the city to issue the lease-revenue bonds in a principal amount not exceeding $100 million to finance a portion of the sports project.

To offset lease-revenue bond issuance costs, the city would issue tax increment bonds backed by future revenues from the project. The city's total financial commitment to the stadium project would be capped at $100 million, San Francisco officials said.

The entire project is expected to cost $537 million, including $250 million for a proposed stadium for the National Football League's San Francisco 49ers, and $200 million for a proposed entertainment and shopping complex.
Before the board's finance committee endorsed the bond resolution earlier this week, city officials added several amendments designed to protect San Francisco's general fund.

"The proposal has been structured not to hit the general fund so there's no cost to the taxpayer," said Michael Colbruno, spokesman for the 49ers stadium project. "Revenues from the project should offset the cost of the bonds."

The amendments require certification that the total net proceeds of the bonds will not exceed $100 million and require the 49ers to play home games in the stadium until the retirement of the city's debt.
Another amendment states that the city will be responsible for no more than 50 percent of the football-related operations and maintenance expenses at the stadium.
